claims.text: Role in unstable bradycardia: temporizing, w transcutaneous pacing and/or isoproterenol.
claims.quote: Bradycardia: Transcutaneous pacing, atropine, and/or isoproterenol

claims.text: Dose: IV, titrated to HR, PR interval, BP and Sx;
claims.quote: Titrate based on heart rate, PR interval, blood pressure and symptoms.

claims.text: w CAD limit the total dose to 0.03–0.04 mg/kg (2–3 mg) to ⍉tachy raising myocard O2 demand.
claims.quote: When the recurrent use of atropine is essential in patients with coronary artery disease, the total dose should be restricted to 2 to 3 mg (maximum 0.03 to 0.04 mg/kg) to avoid the detrimental effects of atropine-induced tachycardia on myocardial oxygen demand.

claims.text: SE (antimuscarinic): dry mouth, blurred vision, photophobia and tachy are common;
claims.quote: Dryness of the mouth, blurred vision, photophobia and tachycardia commonly occur.

claims.text: constipation and difficulty urinating may occur in the elderly.
claims.quote: Constipation and difficulty in micturition may occur in elderly patients.

claims.text: OD: a short-acting barbiturate or diazepam for marked excitement and convulsions;
claims.quote: In the event of toxic overdosage, a short acting barbiturate or diazepam may be given as needed to control marked excitement and convulsions.

claims.text: physostigmine 1–4 mg by slow IV inj rapidly reverses delirium and coma,
claims.quote: Physostigmine, given as an atropine antidote by slow intravenous injection of 1 to 4 mg (0.5 to 1 mg in pediatric populations), rapidly abolishes delirium and coma caused by large doses of atropine.

claims.text: but it = rapidly destroyed, so repeat doses may be needed.
claims.quote: Since physostigmine is rapidly destroyed, the patient may again lapse into coma after one to two hours, and repeated doses may be required.
